why: Making high-contradiction risk an explicit, primary signal (C1) — reinforced by the negation example swap (E4) — caused scorers to avoid cuts that isolate negation/scope or obvious contradiction sites and instead shift cuts to other, weaker junctions (e.g., splitting function words and list items). That redistribution produced a small net loss in H_set (n_worse>n_better) concentrated in longer-latency bins (≤10 and ≤99) with modest harm also for the shortest pieces (≤3), matching the by_bin pattern.
lesson: A later revision should keep contradiction-risk demotion but avoid prompting scorers to systematically relocate cuts into positions that split function words or enumerations and thereby reduce cohesion for longer-latency cut sets.
